input.summary:
Roofs part built: shop flat-parapet roof (y6) from roof.json and service block roof (y8, x24..32 z24..33, no west overhang) via roof() in parts/roofs.mjs, with palette-only stone materials and a rooftop rail.
Two hvac_unit rooftop units at (26,28) and (29,28) on the service deck, y9..10.
make.sh saved a whole build.nbt; Roofs part placed 202 cells with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; check reports 0 floating and 0 unsupported; renders read as flat roofs with the taller service block and HVAC.
left: ROOF_SINGLE_MATERIAL warning on both flat decks (the deck reads as one tone); a flat deck is intended, so left as is.
The shop roof's north overhang at z=23 sits at y6..7 and the keep box protects the MART lettering cells, but the lettering part must still check it lands on those keep cells.
The service roof is laid in parts/roofs.mjs rather than roof.json because runParts takes one roof spec with a single y; plan.md Notes records this.

waste.what: Testing roof material variants one at a time: stone, mix and trim choices each needed a dry-run to see which blocks came out off-palette (smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab, stone_slab from the modern preset defaults).
waste.tool: A `mcd roof --spec ... --dry-run --palette palette.json` mode that lists off-palette blocks and suggests the palette-matching trim/eave/ridge per preset, plus the keys the spec's material object accepts.

waste.what: The second roof at a different y had to be hand-wired in roofs.mjs because runParts lays one roof.json; the spec keys (footprint, keep, overhang per side) were worked out by reading roofs.mjs.
waste.cost: About 3 minutes reading roof() options and writing a direct call
waste.tool: runParts accepting a list of roof specs (roof: ["roof.json", "roof-service.json"]) or a per-footprint y in the roof spec, with the spec keys documented in references/toolkit.md.
